text: A new Staking page manages delegated coins, including those of imported delegated keys: track staking balances and rewards, and unstake a chosen amount or the available maximum while keeping the remainder delegated, with resumable submission. Send uses only ordinary coins in seed and imported-key wallets and guides you to Staking when those funds are insufficient. Staking has its own network icon, distinct from Coins in the sidebar, and its How it works button explains staking in a dialog. Staking opens with a summary of the delegated balance that shows what can be unstaked now, what unlocks after a stake and when, what is pending, frozen or reserved, and the latest reward; per-key cards appear when several keys hold coins. Unstaking, token returns and recovery transfers each run in their own dialog through amount, review and result steps. Amount fields match Send, with the coin symbol and Max inside; empty fields stay neutral until review is requested. Reviews keep their explanations and require only the confirmation button, without acknowledgement checkboxes. Results distinguish pending transactions, confirmations and errors, and errors stay with their dialog or operation and are brought into view on small screens. Unstake ignores outside clicks and keeps entered amounts for each key when closed or revisited from review. Transaction details remain readable when staking recovery fails, with incomplete ownership explicitly marked. Imported delegated keys keep returned coins and change on their ordinary address. Transactions up to 2 MiB can be sent, so larger Falcon transfers no longer hit the former 100 KB limit. Larger staking maximum transfers remain split into separately reviewed parts, and saved large transactions can be restored safely. Unused change addresses remain recoverable after rejected transfers. Pending operations keep explicit reservations, allow pausing retries and reviewing a competing recovery transfer, and no longer block sending during background checks. Staking tokens can be returned to an ordinary address using ordinary coins for network fees. Coins exposes staking outputs for unfreezing, and balances distinguish reservations from freezes. Incomplete staking recovery preserves read access with a warning while blocking spending. Repeated Escape cannot dismiss a busy staking dialog, and successful refreshes clear temporary errors. Recovery transfers can now compete with their original pending transaction even when its inputs are hidden from the available-coin list, with ownership and spending checks before submission. Operations that need a decision appear above the summary with their action. Activity lists operations newest first with their status in words and expandable details, showing five at a time with Show more. Activity also includes confirmed transactions found in the blockchain, including deposits missing from the local journal. Matching transactions appear once per staking address. Discovered entries show balance changes, distinguish staking rewards from restaked coins, and remain read-only. Partial history is identified, and chain reorganizations remove orphaned entries. Unavailable service commissions are omitted. Conflicting staking operations continue to be checked after chain reorganizations and wallet restarts; unresolved inputs are reserved again with automatic resubmission paused. Sending requests change addresses only when needed, so an occupied unused branch no longer blocks a transfer and transactions without change need no new address.
